topics.topic: Decide whether schema SQL names come from imported config constants or are fixed literals
questions: Must config be added to IMPORTS so its persistence constants can be referenced, or must the config.persistence references be removed in favor of the required fixed SQL names?

judgement.why: The topic asks the same question on unchanged text as prior judgement P1.

precedent.topic: Whether to use fixed table names or supply and use config.persistence references
quotes: create_budget_schema: [CONFIG_REFERENCE] MUST idempotently create only the tables budget_versions (= config.persistence.budget_version_table_name) and section_plans (= config.persistence.section_plan_table_name), written as fixed names in the SQL text, with columns corresponding one-to-one to BudgetVersion and SectionPlan fields; version_id and plan_id are primary keys, (version_id, section_id) is unique, and nullable model fields remain nullable.
Use only the IMPORTS listed above plus required standard library imports.
precedent.why: The prompt explicitly requires the literal fixed table names in SQL and permits no unlisted config-module import.

topics.topic: Resolve the conflict over the required object annotation for connection
questions: Must connection retain the contract-required object annotation, or must the prohibition against object annotations change?
Must connection retain the contract-required object annotation, or must the prohibition against object annotations change?

quotes: def __init__(self, connection: object, context: AuditRepositoryContext) -> None
Import from IMPORTS every symbol the module uses, including symbols used only in annotations, and annotate each parameter with the type its CONTRACTS signature declares, never object or nothing.
judgement.why: The declared signatures require object annotations for connection, while the general annotation instruction forbids object annotations.

questions: Must authenticate_staff ignore email_verified_at, or must an account without email_verified_at be unable to authenticate?
Must authenticate_staff ignore email_verified_at, or is an unverified account forbidden from authenticating?
Must authenticate_staff require email_verified_at, or must the claim that an unverified account could never authenticate be removed or revised?

judgement.why: This asks the same question about unchanged text as P2.

quotes: authenticate_staff: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST normalize email, accept only an account whose status is StaffStatus.ACTIVE with a matching password, deciding nothing on email_verified_at, issue a hashed fixed-expiry session, audit success or concealed failure, and never reveal which check failed.
precedent.why: Authentication must ignore email_verified_at and depend on active status and a matching password.

precedent.topic: Whether session resolution must reject an active staff account without email verification
quotes: resolve_staff_session: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST parse the R17 selector, verify its secret hash, fixed expiry, revocation and that the account status is StaffStatus.ACTIVE before returning StaffActorContext, deciding nothing on email_verified_at; any failure raises AuthenticationRejected.

topics.topic: Define validation versus already-initialized-store error precedence during administrator bootstrap
questions: Must email/password validation occur before the only persistence call, or must an already initialized store take precedence even when those inputs are invalid; if completion must take precedence, how can it be determined without querying persistence or passing an unvalidated account to create_if_empty?

quotes: MUST normalize the supplied email and validate the supplied password through the existing staff identity input boundary, hash that password exactly as supplied through the credential boundary, build the account with StaffRole.ADMINISTRATOR, StaffStatus.ACTIVE, a set email_verified_at and created_by None, and its audit record with ActorKind.SYSTEM and no actor_id, key_version or project_id, AuditAction.STAFF_CREATE, AuditEntityKind.STAFF_ACCOUNT, AuditResult.SUCCESS and no reason_code, and hand both to the port in one call.
judgement.why: The prescribed sequence validates the inputs before constructing the account and handing it to the port, so invalid input takes precedence over detecting an initialized store.

topics.topic: Define whether storage exceptions must be sanitized to prevent password-hash leakage
questions: If a storage failure's exception message contains the password hash from the StaffAccount passed to the port, must the exception be propagated unchanged or altered to prevent the hash from reaching an exception message?

quotes: MUST retain the supplied password only in hashed form and MUST NOT let that password or its hash reach standard output, standard error, a log, an audit record, a returned value or an exception message.
A genuine storage failure MUST propagate unchanged and MUST NOT be turned into either refusal.
judgement.why: An unchanged storage exception containing the hash necessarily exposes it in an exception message, which the security requirement forbids.

topics.topic: Whether financial validation occurs inside the transaction or pre-transaction validation errors are exempt from rollback
questions: A FinancialValidationError is a BaseException raised before any transaction exists, so it cannot be rolled back; must the rollback rule apply only after a transaction has opened, or must validation occur inside the transaction?

Amount validation can fail before the shared transaction and its repositories exist; must “any failure” be limited to failures after the transaction opens, or must amount validation occur after opening it?
Must FinancialValidationError be raised before any transaction is opened, or is it exempt from the requirement to rollback every BaseException before commit?

quotes: - register_work_payment: [BEHAVIOR] MUST validate the amount through validate_eur_amount with the portal currency EUR and strictly_positive=True before opening any transaction, so a FinancialValidationError changes nothing; payment_id is the replay identity: equal payment_id/content returns existing, conflict changes nothing, and a new payment plus AuditAction.PAYMENT_REGISTER audit commits atomically without creating an invoice/accounting posting.

- register_work_payment: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST rollback and re-raise every BaseException before commit; replay MUST rollback once and return without audit, while a successful commit MUST not be followed by rollback.
judgement.divergence: One implementation validates before opening a transaction and therefore raises FinancialValidationError without rollback; another opens the transaction before validation so it can rollback that BaseException. The store and transaction owner notice whether a transaction is opened and rolled back.
judgement.why: The unconditional requirement to rollback every BaseException before commit conflicts with the requirement that financial validation occur before any transaction exists.
